attempts.operation: B9 training start: windowless scheduling slowdown
attempts.failure_signature: Started windowless from a shell, the unchanged B3 recipe ran at 0.36 s per chip, not B4's 0.18 s. GPU utilisation was 22-47% and CPU load 6%: the single training thread was the limit.
attempts.diagnosis: Windows schedules the windowless interpreter at low quality of service (efficiency cores). Pinning to logical processors 0-15, the performance cores of this i7-14700K, or turning power throttling off for the process, restores 0.18 to 0.20 s per chip. B3 run 1 shows the same two rates in its own journal (0.19 s for the first steps, 0.35 s afterwards).

bounded_comparison.data: Karnataka TRAIN only, unchanged B3 recipe, 200 chips each

attempts.fix: The launch supervisor pins itself to mask 0xFFFF; the trainer and its DEV scorer inherit it. This is a process attribute, not a recipe or system setting.
attempts.result: The B9 run of six epochs held 0.2108 s per chip (median 0.1864) between its DEV pauses; at the slow rate eight epochs would have taken 735 minutes against a 480-minute budget.
attempts.decision: Start long training through scripts/ml/launch_extra_train.py or with the same pinning. A venv python.exe is a launcher stub: affinity or priority set on it does not reach the interpreter.
